_comment: catalog.ucsd.edu is the source of truth for prerequisites; refresh/ parses it into data/catalog.json.
This file records the reviewed decisions the parsed catalog cannot carry: sequence orderings
that a placement exam can bypass, owner-confirmed readings of ambiguous lines, carried-over
substitutes and advisories, and edges deliberately not adopted (rejected_edges is documentation
only; build() does not apply it), each with its reason.

add_edges.why: The catalog lets AP credit stand in for MATH 20A, so 20B's requirement is not a hard course prerequisite — but for anyone who does take 20A the ordering still binds, and a planner that allowed 20B first would be wrong for every student who has not tested out.
Same as MATH 20A -> 20B: satisfiable by AP credit, binding for anyone taking the course.
MATH 189 lists MATH 18 and a probability course; the department also requires MATH 20C, which the catalog line omits.
The catalog line reads '(… or CSE 151A and DSC 106)', which taken literally makes DSC 106 optional. The owner confirmed on 2026-11-13 that DSC 180A requires DSC 106.

rejected_edges.why: Linear algebra does not require second-quarter calculus. Present in the old hand-written table; unsupported by the catalog.
Redundant. CSE 151A requires a programming background, and CSE 12 already satisfies that group.
Redundant. Covered by the <probability> group, which MATH 180A satisfies.
CSE 15L lists no prerequisite in the catalog.
Modelled instead as the <qualifying elective> group, so DSC 140B and DSC 148 count equally rather than all three being required.

The catalog names MATH 20A as one way to clear MATH 18's placement requirement, not as an ordering. Treating it as an edge would force linear algebra after third-quarter calculus, which is the opposite of how the major is advised.

substitutes.why: Carried over from the hand-written dataset (before 2026-11); the catalog prerequisite line does not state it. Owner to confirm.
